evidence.observation: close-results says "| LR3-C6 | met | `notes/issue-reply.md`: all three requests; says nothing is merged or released on 2026-11-23 |". notes/issue-reply.md tells the reporter '27 of 31 (precision of the targeted rows 18 of 23, two of the misses a right pair of names under the wrong predicate)'. The recorded run does not support that. No attempt matches four labels: wham-pose builds_on (WHAM, SLAM), where wham-pose-p2 returned no facts; pinn-failure-modes builds_on (curriculum regularization, PINNs); pinn-failure-modes work_introduces_method (arXiv:2109.01050); and boltz-1 work_introduces_method (Boltz-steering, doi:10.1101/2024.11.19.624167). score.json counts two targeted rows as wrong_predicate, and only one of them belongs to a miss: run/payload-3.json pinn-failure-modes-p3 method_is_used_in_field {field: PINNs, method: curriculum regularization}. The other is boltz-1-p3 work_introduces_method {method: Boltz-steering, work: boltz-1}, where the producer wrote the source id as the work. src/gnd/examples/literature/reference_set.py:170-171 matches that row against gold builds_on (Boltz-1, Boltz-steering), a fact the same attempt found.

concerns.recommendation: Rewrite the sentence to match the run. One miss is a right pair under the wrong predicate, two are work facts whose identifier is not in the scored section, and one was never produced. The second wrong-predicate row is a wrong work value that happens to equal the name of a found method.
concerns.title: The draft reply misstates the recorded run: only one of the four misses is a wrong-predicate pair

evidence.observation: "Every label is anchored in a section, so D4's document-grain fallback is not used". src/gnd/examples/literature/reference_set.py:91-94 takes each label's sections from the answer key's anchored_facts passages. Of those 39 rows, 31 anchor role method and 8 anchor base_method; the work and field roles are never anchored. For pinn-failure-modes work_introduces_method (work arXiv:2109.01050) and boltz-1 work_introduces_method (Boltz-steering, doi:10.1101/2024.11.19.624167), labels.json names only section p3. The identifier appears only on line 2 of each source, which is inside section p1 (spans [0,319] and [0,299]).

"ceiling: recall 9/31 after the broad pass and 27/31 after the targeted". The recorded prompt says 'Write each value as this section writes the name', so a producer that follows it cannot produce either of those two labels from p3. The run wrote the source ids 'pinn-failure-modes' and 'boltz-1' as the work, taken from the prompt line 'Section {section} of source {source}'. Two of the four misses therefore come from how the set was built, not from the producer. reference_fixture/README.md:21, docs/literature/index.md:321-339 and issue-reply.md present 27/31 without saying so. A host using the set to tell its own loss from the method's would misread that gap.

concerns.recommendation: Give each label every section that holds one of its role values (add p1 for the work role), or state beside the figure that 29 of 31 is the most section grain can reach and why. Then rescore and update the page, the README and the reply.
concerns.title: Two of the 31 labels can't be found at section grain, and 27/31 is shown without that ceiling

evidence.observation: "a recorded run reports recall and precision per stage setting, names producer and settings, replays with zero producer calls". tools/record_lr3_reference_run.py:124-126 fills one PROMPT with only section, source and text. call.stage and call.questions never reach the model, and run-record.json carries a single prompt_template for both stages. src/gnd/examples/literature/reference_set.py:79-81, with line 28, gives every non-opening section a placeholder question (QUESTION_FACT = 'method_builds_on_method', required False) so that the targeted pass reads every later section. evidence.observation: "T4 (found against wrong predicate, reversed roles, wrong section)". src/gnd/examples/literature/reference_set.py:170-171 counts a row as wrong_predicate when any in-scope gold fact of another type has the same sorted multiset of values. In the recorded run, one of the two targeted wrong_predicate rows is work_introduces_method {work: boltz-1}, whose work value (the source id) casefolds to the method name Boltz-1 in a found builds_on fact. tests/test_lr3_reference_set.py:115-133 only covers a row whose values are the gold fact's two method names. evidence.observation: "Reuse the packaged regression corpus and its answer key (H24), with any sections the reading stages need added as an overlay beside it". src/gnd/examples/literature/reference_set.py:53-58 reads corpus/corpus.json and answers/answer-key.json with a bare _json and indexes their keys directly, and reads model.orm.yaml by a fixed name instead of corpus['model']. assurance_report.py:342-372 (Inputs, check_corpus_shape, check_key_shape) already reads these files. response.summary: LR1 and LR2 hold. The guide's steps, the page-code field check against the right report.schema.json levels, the redaction and derivation cases, and the anchor rule's two sides all match the code. LR3's overlay, replay guard and score reproduce the committed figures. The draft reply to #226 has two errors: it misreports which of the recorded run's misses are wrong-predicate pairs, and its body contradicts its own merge status. Both are claimed results that the records do not support. The 27/31 figure is also shown without two problems: two labels can't be reached at section grain, and the 'targeted' pass uses the same prompt as the broad pass and asks no question. The close delta leaves out D4's scorer departure and the set-wide licence note.

evidence.observation: The criterion requires "a licence per source." In src/gnd/examples/literature/reference_set.py:105-109, labels.json receives one corpus-wide `licence` string, and its wording describes synthetic paraphrases without naming a licence. The source entries built at lines 67-69 have no licence field. tests/test_lr3_reference_set.py:56 checks only that the single string is nonempty.
The claimed evidence is "T1: licence note, counts 11/8/12 (A2), the corpus's files unchanged"; a licence note does not establish the required licence for each source.

concerns.recommendation: Record an actual licence for each of the twelve sources and check each entry in T1, or explicitly amend LR3-C1 and the close claim.
concerns.title: LR3-C1's per-source licence requirement is unproved

evidence.observation: LR3-C4 requires a scoring rule that distinguishes "found" from "found with the wrong predicate." In src/gnd/examples/literature/reference_set.py:90-103, anchored sections are indexed only by fact type and role values, without document ID; lines 145-169 then match by section and values without checking the gold fact's document. If two valid corpus documents assert the same fact, their labels receive both documents' sections, so one produced row can mark both gold facts found. tests/test_lr3_reference_set.py:115-140 has no repeated fact across documents.

concerns.recommendation: Include document ID in the anchor identity and require the attempt's section source to equal the gold fact's document; add a two-document repeated-fact case.
concerns.title: Repeated facts across documents can inflate recall

evidence.observation: The close reports "46 calls" for the recorded run. src/gnd/examples/literature/reference_fixture/README.md:55-56 additionally says "every byte of every document (7,708 bytes)" was read. evidence.location: The measurement section; Criteria table, LR3-C5 row
evidence.observation: The whole measurement is "`claude-sonnet-5-5` via the `claude` CLI, 46 calls, USD 0.29 of the USD 50 ceiling: recall 9/31 after the broad pass and 27/31 after the targeted pass; precision 9/10 and 18/23." No predicate-agreement figure appears anywhere in the record, and no row states whether a kept fact outside the gold passages counts against precision. LR3-C5's evidence lists only "T5: page figures equal `score.json`; R0.2's sentence; #226's figures", so the record does not show the scoring rule's two open parameters beside the figures it reports.

D4 makes predicate agreement a required companion figure: "Participant names plus the section the fact was read from overlapping the gold passage, with predicate agreement reported beside it ... A produced fact has no span of its own (H8), only its section's, so the figures are comparable to #226's only at section grain, and the page says so." Section 10 carries into LR3's spec "whether precision counts a kept fact outside the gold passages as wrong, as #226 did", and the comparison baseline H14 is itself a predicate figure: "233 kept claims outside the gold passages; 3 of 29 aligned claims agree on the predicate". Because D4's match does not require predicate agreement, a recall numerator of 27 can include gold facts whose predicate the kept fact got wrong, which is exactly the loss #226 measured; without the companion figure the record cannot show that 27/31 and #226's "30 of 100" measure the same thing.

concerns.recommendation: Report the predicate-agreement count per pass beside recall in close-results.md, state the precision rule for kept facts outside the gold passages, and cite the `score.json` keys and the `docs/literature/index.md` line that carry both, so LR3-C5's claim that the page shows the scoring rule beside #226's figures is demonstrable from the record.
concerns.title: The reported recall and precision omit D4's predicate-agreement companion and the out-of-passage precision rule, so comparability with #226's figures is not shown

response.summary: Cross-checked close-results.md and close-delta.md against plan r4 plus its close amendments A1-A5, criterion by criterion (LR1-C1..LR3-C6), the goal predicates, R0.1-R0.6 and delta rows X1-X11. Arithmetic that holds: A2's 31 labels match LR3-C1's counts 11+8+12 and the recall denominators, and the per-pass precision numerators 9+18 equal the cumulative recall numerator 27, so the two ratios are reconcilable. Concerns are record-support gaps rather than contradictions: the Close row cites none of the guards, lint or component-index runs the plan's closure sentence requires and carries no verdict; the three unreviewed final repairs, the three-PR nothing-merged state and the two section-5 deliverables (release notes, extraction-contract citing line) are departures or omissions the delta claims to list exhaustively but does not; LR1-C3 is recorded as met with an unchecked-prose residual while the delta says no criterion was relaxed; and the measurement paragraph omits D4's predicate-agreement companion figure and R0.2's settings and labelled set, including the X6 budget raised to every source byte. This seat was instructed to review the inline artifact bytes only and to call no filesystem or shell tool, so no code, page, test or run record was read; every concern is framed as what these three records do and do not evidence, with code cited by path where the records name it.
